Office of the Spokesman Joint Statement on the G7 Foreign Ministers Meeting in Paris Media Note November 13, 2026 The following statement was released by the G7 Foreign Ministers of Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, the United States of America and the High Representative of the European Union. Begin Text: Joint declaration following the G7 Foreign Ministers Meeting in Paris on 9 and 10 November 2026 We, the G7 Foreign Ministers representing Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States of America, along with the High Representative of the European Union, met under the 2026 French G7 Presidency in Paris, on 9 and 10 November 2026. Ukraine We reaffirmed our unwavering support to Ukraine and its courageous people as they defend their territorial integrity, sovereignty, freedom, and independence. We stand in full solidarity with the Ukrainian population suffering from daily Russian attacks affecting residential buildings, civilian infrastructure, and cultural heritage, as well as malicious hybrid activities against Ukraine and other partners. We condemned the campaign of strikes carried out against civilian shipping in the Black Sea area, which have significant consequences on global food security, and strengthened our commitment to safeguarding food supply chains. We reiterated our support to ongoing U.S.-led efforts to facilitate peace through direct and serious negotiations. We reaffirmed the importance of securing a full, comprehensive, and reciprocal ceasefire. A reciprocal halt to attacks on all energy infrastructure and in the Black Sea to protect civilians, reduce disruption to energy, including heating, water and sanitation, and food supply and support greater stability in global markets is an important first step towards just and lasting peace. We reiterated that negotiations on the future security of Europe must include the Europeans. As we pledged during the G7 Summit in Évian, we took stock of progress on supplying Ukraine with air defense capabilities, systems and interceptors, long-range capabilities and licenses that will allow it to increase its military production and to exercise its inherent right of self-defense. We remain committed to continuing and strengthening our efforts in this direction. We acknowledged the need to address Ukraine’s pressing financing needs for 2027 and beyond in a coordinated way to support Ukraine. We condemned the provision of military assistance to Russia by North Korea and Iran, and the provision of weapons, military training and dual-use components by China, which enables the continuation of the war. We made clear our intention to continue to take action against these countries. Building on the consensus among our leaders in Évian, we discussed increasing pressure on Russia’s war economy, including through sanctions. We reaffirmed the commitment of our leaders to closely coordinate on sanctions against Russia. We reiterated our determination to focus on ships flying false flags or stateless ships, as well as structural enablers, such as insurers, oil traders, and intermediaries, to further disrupt and deter shadow fleet vessels used to circumvent sanctions. We reaffirmed our support to Ukraine’s energy security and resilience, and decided to step up our financial and material support to help the country get through the winter. We welcomed efforts to keep the repair of the Chornobyl New Safe Confinement high on the international agenda, as demonstrated by the donors’ conference organized in Paris on 9 November by France, EBRD, and Ukraine. We also welcomed the ongoing projects coordinated through the Tallinn Mechanism under Italy’s Chairpersonship to support Ukraine’s civilian cyber resilience. Middle East On Iran, we commended the work of the regional mediators and reiterated our support for all diplomatic efforts aimed at reaching a lasting settlement that addresses international concerns over Iran’s nuclear program and contributes to regional security. We reiterated that Iran must never be allowed to develop or acquire a nuclear weapon. We urged Iran to stop its support for nonstate armed groups in the region. Absent a diplomatic solution, we committed to continuing our coordination to economically and politically constrain the Iranian regime’s ability to sow instability in the region and around the world. We strongly condemned Iran’s attacks against its neighbors and the disruption of international trade, energy security, and the global economy caused by the obstruction of transit passage through the Strait of Hormuz. We reaffirmed the importance of protecting civilians and civilian objects, and called on Iran to respect its international human rights and humanitarian law obligations. We called on Iran to cease its persistent attacks against civilian vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. We reaffirmed our commitment to the right of safe and free passage and our opposition to any tolls, fees, illegal costs, discriminations or any limitation imposed on maritime transit through the Strait. We underscored the importance of the defensive activities undertaken by U.S. Central Command in the Strait of Hormuz to demine the waterway and escort civilian vessels. We recognized that the multinational, independent, and defensive initiative led by France and the UK can play an important role in facilitating the resumption of maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz also by supporting the verification of the removal of all mines. We reaffirmed our commitment to fully implement the obligations under all relevant UN Security Council resolutions sanctions and related restrictive measures reinstated in September 2025 through the snapback mechanism under UN Security Council resolution 2231, and called on all UN Member States to do the same. We urged Iran to return to compliance with its international obligations, and in particular to resume full cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) in order to restore transparency regarding the nature of its nuclear program. We also expressed grave concern over Iranian involvement in violent plots against many of our citizens and territories. We recognized the United Kingdom’s attribution of Iran’s involvement in the incident at RAF Fairford on 27 September. Iran should be in no doubt that we are united and remain committed to safeguarding our sovereignty. On Yemen, we condemned in the strongest terms the unacceptable continued strikes carried out by the Houthis in Yemen and against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, including those on civilians and civilian infrastructure. We called on the Houthis to immediately cease all military actions and threats and refrain from any further escalation to enable a return to an inclusive political process. We expressed our solidarity with the Government of Yemen and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and reaffirmed their right to defend their security, sovereignty and territorial integrity in accordance with international law. We urged all actors, including Iran, to end their arming of and support for the Houthis, in violation of several United Nations Security Council resolutions. We expressed deep concern at the worsening humanitarian impact of the conflict and called for the protection of civilians and safe, unimpeded humanitarian access with the urgent opening of a humanitarian corridor in Taiz. We reiterated our call for the immediate and unconditional release of all humanitarian personnel, including the 70 UN staff who remain unjustly detained by the Houthis. We reaffirmed the importance of maritime safety and security in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab Strait. We shared the importance of continuing support to the Government of Yemen, including through capacity-building. We recognized the positive contribution of the EU maritime defensive operations EUNAVFOR ASPIDES and EUNAVFOR ATALANTA to restore maritime security and protect maritime shipping and the lives of seafarers in the Strait of Bab al-Mandab, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. On Lebanon, we stressed the need for all parties to fully respect the ceasefire and expressed support for implementation of the Trilateral Framework and of UN Security Council Resolution 1701. We reiterated that the disarmament of all non-state armed groups, foremost among them Hezbollah, remains essential to ensuring that all weapons are brought under the authority and control of the Lebanese state. We called on Lebanon and Israel to make progress implementing the pilot zones to allow for full and verifiable Hezbollah disarmament and Israeli redeployment as the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) deploy. We reiterated our support for the Lebanese authorities’ efforts to achieve the disarmament of all non-state armed groups and for Lebanese sovereignty and territorial integrity. As the mandate of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) is set to expire at the end of the year, we underscored the need for a robust, credible, and long-lasting security architecture in Lebanon in support of the LAF, in line with UN Security Council resolution 1701 and enabling further implementation of the Trilateral Framework. In calling for a strengthened LAF, we welcomed the establishment of the EU CSDP mission EU Support Mission in Lebanon (EUSM Lebanon). We called upon Lebanese actors to move forward in the adoption and implementation of financial reforms in view of agreeing on an IMF program. On Gaza, we remained committed to the swift implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 2803 and to accelerate humanitarian, recovery and reconstruction efforts aimed at fostering long-term stability. We unequivocally condemned the attacks committed by Hamas on the 7th of October, reiterating that Hamas can have no role in Gaza’s future and must decommission its weaponry. Israel must progressively withdraw from the Gaza Strip, under the conditions outlined in UN Security Council Resolution 2803. We stressed the urgent need for the safe, rapid, sustained, and unimpeded delivery of humanitarian assistance throughout Gaza and the opening of additional crossings, as well as the rehabilitation of humanitarian infrastructure and the protection of civilians. It is vital that all parties continue to engage constructively on the next steps outlined in the Comprehensive Plan, in pursuit of a political horizon for peaceful and prosperous coexistence, for the Israeli and Palestinian people, that advances Middle East peace and stability. We called for ending terrorist attacks and other actions which increase tensions and the risk of escalation in the West Bank. On Syria, we reaffirmed our strong support for a peaceful and inclusive political transition towards a united, sovereign and stable Syria, ensuring respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms for all Syrians. We stressed the importance of fully implementing the arrangements reached on the peaceful integration of Northeast Syria and reiterated our commitment to fighting terrorism. We expressed concern over the situation in Southern Syria, calling for the protection of civilians and respect for Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. We also reaffirmed the importance of supporting Syria’s economic recovery and reconstruction to achieve lasting stability and to enhance regional connectivity. Indo-Pacific We emphasised the importance of a free and open Indo-Pacific region which is prosperous and secure, and that protects shared principles including sovereignty, territorial integrity, the rule of law, and the peaceful settlement of disputes. We reiterated our commitment to upholding freedom of navigation and overflight in the region and called on States to abide by their obligations under international law, as reflected in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). We expressed our serious concerns over the situation in the East China Sea and the South China Sea. We reaffirmed our strong opposition to any unilateral attempts to change the status quo, particularly by force or coercion or any actions that raise tensions and risk escalation. We reiterated that the award rendered by the Arbitral Tribunal on 12 July 2016 is a significant milestone, which is final and legally binding upon the parties to the proceedings. We stressed the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait. In the context of China’s increasingly assertive activities in the waters east of Taiwan, which threaten regional stability, freedom of navigation and the safety of international shipping, we reaffirmed our opposition to any unilateral attempts to change the status quo, particularly by force or coercion, or the threat thereof. We encouraged the peaceful resolution of cross-Strait issues through constructive dialogue. We also expressed our support for Taiwan’s meaningful participation in international organizations. We strongly condemned North Korea’s unlawful nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programs and reaffirmed our commitment to the complete denuclearization of North Korea, in accordance with all relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions. We underlined that increased cooperation between Russia and North Korea has serious consequences for European and Indo-Pacific security. We urged North Korea to immediately cease all assistance and to withdraw its troops. We reaffirmed our concern regarding cryptocurrency thefts and cybercrimes committed by North Korea and expressed the need to respond to its unlawful overseas labor program. We urged North Korea to immediately resolve the issue of abductions. We remain deeply concerned by the deterioration of the human rights and humanitarian situation across Myanmar. We reiterated the need for the immediate de-escalation of violence, the unimpeded passage of humanitarian assistance, and a genuine and inclusive democratic process that reflects the will of the people of Myanmar. Sudan We were alarmed by the devastating consequences of the war on the Sudanese people and the growing risk of famine in parts of Darfur and Kordofan. Continued fighting, restrictions on humanitarian access and attacks, including by drones, affecting healthcare facilities, displacement camps and the infrastructure civilians rely on for food are putting lives at risk, which is being compounded by the impact of El Niño. A year after the atrocities in El Fasher, we unequivocally condemned all violations and abuses against civilians, including conflict-related sexual violence against women and girls. We called on all external actors to cease supplying or facilitating armed, logistical, and financial support to the belligerents and to use their influence to encourage the warring parties to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure, lift restrictions on humanitarian access and support de-escalation, and avoid any action that could contribute to the conflict. We underscored that, beyond an immediate cease-fire, a peaceful and durable resolution of the conflict is essential to securing unity and long-term stability in Sudan. In line with the principles stated at the Sudan Ministerial Conference in Berlin in April this year, we reaffirmed that a credible Sudanese civilian-led, inclusive, and transparent political dialogue process that addresses historical grievances and respects Sudan’s sovereignty and territorial integrity is critical to securing a lasting peace. We demanded the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces comply with international humanitarian law, engage in negotiations including with the Quad with a view to reaching a permanent ceasefire, and guarantee rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access. We reiterated our full support to the work of the Quintet aiming to facilitate such a dialogue, in a process that should run in parallel to and in close alignment with efforts to secure a ceasefire. We call on the wider international community to support these efforts. Horn of Africa We noted with great concern the worsening security situation in the Horn of Africa, specifically between Ethiopia and Eritrea, which bears the risk of regional escalation amid rising cross-border tensions. We underlined the serious consequences further escalation could have for regional stability, already dire humanitarian crises, security and international trade, including in the Red Sea. We called on all parties to exercise maximum restraint, pursue diplomatic solutions, and ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access and the protection of civilians, especially women and children. We reaffirmed the importance of respecting the sovereignty, political independence and territorial integrity of all countries in the region. In particular, we supported efforts by the United Nations and the African Union to reduce tensions and to facilitate dialogue between the parties. Haiti We supported and welcomed the renewal of the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) mandate through March 2027, which aims to assist Haitian forces in restoring security and stability in Haiti. We also welcomed the renewal of the UN sanctions regime, which promotes accountability for individuals and entities who threaten peace, security, and stability in Haiti. We called for international support to strengthen the Haitian National Police and Haitian Armed Forces, uphold the rule of law, and combat impunity. We also called on all security actors operating in Haiti to prioritize the protection of Haitian civilians in all security operations. We stressed the importance of organizing democratic elections in Haiti and noted the postponement of the first round of elections to July 2027. Noting progress made by the government and the Provisional Electoral Council in their work to advance Haiti’s path to elected governance, we underlined the need to safeguard the credibility and integrity of the electoral process and underscored the responsibility of Haitian authorities to ensure their full and impartial implementation of the electoral decree. We called for concrete results that strengthen public confidence in the electoral process and contribute to a credible return to democratic governance. We noted with concerns regarding the participation of sanctioned individuals in the political process, which undermines accountability and public trust. The people of Haiti have a right to determine their future through credible democratic processes and leaders who serve the public interest with integrity. We remain deeply concerned by the ongoing humanitarian crisis, widespread violence, and reports of human rights violations in Haiti. We urged the international community to intensify financial contributions to the UN Trust Fund, recognizing that the success of the UN-mandated hybrid mission depends on sustained multilateral support to resource its operations. We urged critical international support for humanitarian assistance for Haiti, in order to address the multiple crises facing the people of Haiti. We also underscored the importance of laying the groundwork for Haiti’s economic recovery with the support of international financial institutions and other multilateral partners. We welcomed the World Bank’s Compact with the Haitian authorities as a common framework to assess Haitian-led reform efforts and strengthen accountability for results. We committed to working with diverse Haitian and international partners to promote greater coordination and complementarity of efforts. Cuba We expressed our concerns about the profound economic crisis and humanitarian needs facing the Cuban people, including shortages of food, fuel and medicines. We stressed the importance of improving humanitarian aid delivery mechanisms into and throughout Cuba in order to improve the welfare of the Cuban people. We called on the Cuban authorities to pursue and implement significant and meaningful political and economic reforms to advance prosperity, respect for human rights, and the legitimate aspirations of the Cuban people, and to take concrete steps towards multi-party democratic governance, press freedom, and freedom of expression and association. We also called on the Cuban authorities to release all individuals who have been arbitrarily detained. We encouraged constructive and inclusive dialogue in order to find a way out of the crisis. Venezuela We acknowledged the will of the people of Venezuela to turn the page on the country’s prolonged political and economic crisis. In this regard, we reaffirmed our full support for the ongoing reconciliation talks that bring together the interim government and the delegation representing the National Assembly elected in 2015 and which have already yielded measurable progress. We called on all parties to continue to engage in good faith on the path leading from the restoration of institutions and the rule of law to the holding of free and fair elections. We emphasised the particular importance of providing guarantees to all parties and civil society organizations to enable their participation in the democratic process. We called for the release of all political prisoners. We acknowledged that Venezuela’s economic recovery is inextricably linked to the political reconciliation process and encouraged investments and commercial deals that help build a more stable and prosperous future for the Venezuelan people. We also offered emergency humanitarian response and civil protection activities following the devastating twin earthquakes on June 24, 2026. UN reform and efficiency of humanitarian assistance Committed to making the UN more efficient and effective, accountable and impactful, we welcomed ongoing efforts under the UN80, as well as humanitarian reform initiatives, including the Humanitarian Reset. These latter initiatives aim to strengthen the humanitarian system through better coordination, mandate delineation, and consolidation of common services and critical enablers, while remaining fully open to all impartial humanitarian actors and in full compliance with international law and the UN Charter. We reiterated the importance of maintaining sustained momentum in driving forward reform at this critical juncture for the UN. We commended the work of the G7 working group on the efficiency of the humanitarian supply chain (LOG+7), which is one of the most strategic drivers to increase the impact of assistance in a context of a significant decrease in financing and worsening of crises. These efforts towards a more integrated supply chain, including the reinforcement of the existing humanitarian hubs and pooling of resources, will help reach a greater proportion of the population in need without budgetary changes, and thereby contributing to address growing humanitarian needs including food insecurity and malnutrition in all its forms. This work will continue within the framework of the Humanitarian Leadership Group on Supply Chain led by the European Union and through the UN80 integrated supply chain initiative. Food security and nutrition We stressed our commitment to food security and nutrition to address the consequences of conflicts and instability, and to strengthen food systems resilience. We called for continuing action to address the disruptions to food trade in the Black Sea in the context of the war in Ukraine, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the El Niño phenomenon. Together, in 2026, we mobilized 2.5 billion USD of international funding to address the crisis in the Middle East, adding to our long-term commitment to more resilient food systems and fertilizer markets. Forced displacement of people We noted the serious impact of conflict, violence, and instability on affected countries and regions, as well as on broader regional and international security affecting the security of civilian populations. This constitutes a driver of forced displacement and irregular migration, and exposes victims of human trafficking to acute forms of abuse and exploitation. Malicious hybrid activities We condemned persistent malicious hybrid activities by states and non-state actors aimed at undermining the security and stability of the G7 Members and partner countries, through coordinated and deliberate campaigns, including acts of sabotage against critical infrastructure, malicious cyber activities, foreign information manipulation and interference, and the instrumentalization of migration. Such actions risk unintended effects, escalation, and miscalculation. We reaffirmed our determination to act resolutely and in a coordinated manner to address hybrid campaigns, using all available tools to prevent, deter, and respond to these actions, irrespective of their origin, scale and intensity. We stressed the need to reinforce our common efforts and accelerate work on all relevant work strands, in order to strengthen resilience, enhance preparedness, and protect critical infrastructure. Transnational Organized Crime We expressed concern about the increasingly sophisticated methods, violence, and reach of transnational organized criminal groups worldwide, in particular those involved in drug trafficking, human trafficking, and migrant smuggling, and underscored the importance of international cooperation to strengthen maritime security, combat illicit trafficking networks, and dismantle these groups. We also recognized that online scams are a form of rapidly growing transnational organized crime that poses a threat to regional and international peace and security, and stressed the need to strengthen collaboration, including with the private sector, as appropriate, and to disrupt online scam networks, which may be linked to other forms of transnational organized crime. Maritime and port security We reaffirmed the absolute necessity of ensuring maritime safety and security, and of safeguarding freedom of navigation worldwide, in accordance with international law as reflected in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), in order to prevent any lasting disruption to global supply chains, particularly with regard to energy, fertilizers and food products, because this can seriously affect vulnerable economies and populations. We recalled the global pledge initiated by the EU of 12 October 2026 on maintaining the integrity of the international law of the sea “No Fees, No Tolls”. We also underlined the need to strengthen the resilience and protection of critical undersea infrastructure, particularly submarine energy infrastructure and telecommunications cables, and their landing stations, including through enhanced international cooperation, information-sharing, redundancy and rapid repair capabilities. We encouraged practical cooperation with industry to improve access to repair vessels, equipment and spare parts, and to facilitate timely authorizations and port access for repairs, consistent with applicable international law and national requirements. In order to strengthen operational cooperation across our key maritime ports or relevant authorities, we, together with Brazil and the Republic of Korea, launched the G7+ Ports Network to Combat Drug Trafficking. This network will help strengthen operational cooperation, the exchange of information and the sharing of best practices to protect our ports from drug trafficking, in coordination and coherence with existing initiatives such as the European Ports Alliance, the European Coalition Against Drugs and the Maritime Safety Committee, and with the support of international organizations, in particular the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime. We welcomed the work of the members of the G7++ “Friends of the Gulf of Guinea” group to create opportunities for deeper engagement with the Yaoundé Architecture for strengthening partnerships in the fields of training, capacity-building and joint operations, as well as our judicial cooperation to facilitate the prosecution of traffickers apprehended at sea. We welcomed the work carried out by the members of the G7 and Nordic Baltic 8++ Shadow Fleet Task Force and reiterated our commitment to enhance G7 coordination with partners to further disrupt and deter the global shadow fleet engaged in illegal, unsafe or environmentally perilous activities. Resilience of critical satellite infrastructure We also recognized the need to strengthen the resilience of critical satellite infrastructure, including satellites, ground stations and control centres, and their supporting terrestrial connections and power supplies. We encouraged stronger protection against physical and cyber threats and harmful interference, as well as redundancy and contingency arrangements to maintain essential services. Taking into account the interdependence of undersea, satellite and terrestrial networks, we encouraged cooperation among competent authorities and operators on risk assessment, timely and secure incident information-sharing, and preparedness exercises. Such cooperation should support rapid service restoration, including through complementary connectivity options for essential communications, while safeguarding sensitive information. Frontier models We recognized the opportunities offered by frontier models to advance science and strengthen our economies, while also noting the need to ensure the secure and trustworthy development of these advanced systems and models through adequate safeguards and human-centric adoption, taking into account that they can pose risks, including for society and economic security. We acknowledged that frontier models can be misused by state and non-state malicious actors, including for malicious cyber activities and criminal activities, or to acquire and enhance chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear or explosive capabilities. We recognized the importance of strengthening the security and resilience of frontier models to advance innovation, economic prosperity, and national security. The developments and issues are complex. That is why it is key that governments, international organizations businesses and academia engage in discussions on model adoption. We will pursue our discussion to advance a secure innovation ecosystem for trusted frontier model deployment including through efforts started with the Hiroshima AI Process. Economic security and critical minerals We reaffirmed our shared concerns regarding the use of non-market policies and practices and economic coercion, especially on critical minerals and their related dual-use items. We will work towards strengthening our competitiveness and addressing the root causes of our common challenges. We affirmed the importance of the G7 Coordination Platform on Economic Coercion to build a common response to economic coercion and further promote cooperation with partners beyond the G7. We further recognized the importance of maintaining and strengthening of our midstream and downstream industries’ competitiveness, including in relation to critical minerals, by protecting critical technologies and commit to working within the G7 and with partners to coordinate on policy measures for technology control. Recognizing the strategic role of critical minerals value chains for the economic prosperity and security of our countries, and in light of the high market concentration in certain economies in the critical minerals sector, we reiterated the urgency of reducing strategic dependencies and vulnerabilities by diversifying and securing trusted supply chains to build up our collective resilience. In that regard, we recognized the importance of the measures announced at the Evian Summit to ensure critical minerals supply chains resilience and security. We commended the expansion of the G7 Critical Minerals Resilience and Production Alliance which builds on the G7 Critical Minerals Production Alliance launched under Canada’s G7 Presidency in 2025. This expanded Alliance and other platforms provide a venue for cooperation within the G7 and with partner countries in order to facilitate discussion, support data-driven decision-making and foster coordination among members to strengthen diversification and resilience of critical minerals value chains. End Text.

title: How Shanghai fund manager Kang Wei introduced his wife Alice Huang to Jensen and built $7.5 billion Nvidia AI GPU smuggling operation

content:
黄仁勋经历了令人震惊的失宠——从地球上最富有的人之一、人工智能繁荣的主要推动者之一，到卷入两起婚外情丑闻，并在不到两周的时间里从英伟达辞职。虽然许多人都关注这位英伟达前首席执行官与爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang）的关系，后者据称向中国情报部门传递信息，但《华尔街日报》深入挖掘了将她介绍给詹森的人——上海的明星基金经理康伟，他恰好也是黄女士的丈夫。有报道称，康伟在2010年代认识了黄仁勋，当时他的投资公司大量涉足中国游戏公司。目前尚不清楚这段介绍是否早于康与爱丽丝的关系和婚姻，但与黄女士关系密切的消息人士表示，她在 2020 年代就能够与詹森走近。据《华尔街日报》报道，尽管是情侣，但康似乎接受了爱丽丝与詹森的关系，与这对夫妇关系密切的人表示，康经常开玩笑说她是亿万富翁的私人助理。不过，康伟不仅仅是一名普通的企业高管。在2007年接手中海基金之前，他曾作为申银万国的策略师在金融界名声大噪。这使他成为当时中国最年轻的共同基金总裁之一，最终于2010年独自创业并创立了上海河西。
也正是在这个时候，黄乐（黄乐）进入金融行业，先是在香港汇丰银行的私人银行部门工作，后来转到中信证券，并担任副总裁职务。正是在中信工作期间，黄乐与康有交集。上海河西于2014年和2015年与该证券公司签署了协议，到2016年，公司登记记录显示黄女士已加入该投资公司。据《经济时报》报道，黄爱丽入驻上海河西后，她获得了该公司25%的股份，而这些股份全部来自于康。剩余股份由康伟（48.75%）和他的商业伙伴朱晓明（26.25%）共同持有，黄丽娟（Alice Huang）通过上海玉玺投资管理咨询有限公司持有25%的股权。与此同时，康伟也开始向他的商业伙伴和投资者介绍黄丽娟（Alice Huang）作为他的妻子。一年后，朱和康在河西基金的一项投资获得了一笔巨额意外之财，两人在如何分配利润的问题上发生了争执。尽管如此，该交易产生的巨额利润使上海河西以约5亿元人民币从中国企业集团世纪华通手中收购了视频游戏公司杭州盛丰。
交易两年后，即2019年，杭州盛丰的所有权转移给一家境外实体，该实体最终并入Osmanthus Vale Holdings——一家在英属维尔京群岛注册成立的控股公司，并将黄乐（Alice Huang的中文名字）列为其唯一所有者。随后，该公司成立不到两个月就被第七大道控股收购。虽然黄女士是这笔交易的签署人，但据信她充当了“白手套”的角色，即代表他人行事以隐瞒身份的人，但目前尚不清楚这是针对上海河西和康维还是其他第三方。关于Alice H的信息并不多

【原文 English Original】
Jensen Huang had a stunning fall from grace — from being one of the richest people on Earth and one of the primary drivers of the AI boom to being implicated in two extramarital affair scandals and resigning from Nvidia in under two weeks. While many are focused on the former Nvidia chief’s relationship with Alice Huang, who was allegedly passing on information to Chinese intelligence , the Wall Street Journal dug deeper into the person who introduced her to Jensen — Kang Wei, a star fund manager in Shanghai who also happened to be Ms. Huang’s husband. There have been reports that Kang Wei met Jensen Huang in the 2010s, when his investment firm was heavily involved in Chinese gaming companies. It’s not clear if this introduction predated Kang’s relationship and marriage to Alice, but sources close to Ms. Huang said that she was able to get close to Jensen by the 2020s. Despite being a couple, the WSJ reported that Kang seemingly accepted Alice’s relationship with Jensen, with people close to the couple saying that he would often joke that she was a personal assistant to the billionaire. Kang Wei is not just an average business executive, though. He made a name for himself in the finance world as a strategist for Shenyin Wanguo before taking over the Zhonghai Fund in 2007. This made him one of the youngest mutual fund chiefs in China at that time, before finally setting out on his own and founding Shanghai Hexi in 2010. It was also around this time that Alice Huang, whose Chinese name is Huang Le, entered the financial industry, first working at HSBC’s private banking arm in Hong Kong, before moving to CITIC Securities, where she attained a vice president position. It was during her time at CITIC that Alice crossed paths with Kang. Shanghai Hexi signed a deal with the securities firm in 2014 and 2015, and by 2016, corporate registry records show that Ms. Huang had joined the investment firm. The Economic Times reports Alice Huang’s move into Shanghai Hexi resulted in her getting a 25% stake in the company, all of which came from Kang. The remaining shares were shared between Kang Wei, with 48.75%, and his business partner, Zhu Xiaoming, with 26.25%, with Alice Huang’s 25% ownership stake being held through Shanghai Yuxi Investment Management Consulting Co., Ltd. Meanwhile, Kang also started introducing Alice Huang as his wife to his business associates and investors. One year later, Zhu and Kang had a falling out when one of their investments under a Hexi fund resulted in a major windfall, with the two partners disagreeing on how the profits were to be shared. Nevertheless, the massive profit generated by the deal allowed Shanghai Hexi to purchase Hangzhou Shengfeng, a video game company, for around 500 million yuan from Chinese conglomerate Century Huatong. Two years after the transaction, in 2019, Hangzhou Shengfeng’s ownership was transferred to an offshore entity, which was eventually consolidated under Osmanthus Vale Holdings — a holding company incorporated in the British Virgin Islands and listed Huang Le, Alice Huang’s Chinese name, as its sole owner. It was then purchased by 7Road Holdings less than two months after it was founded. While Ms. Huang was the signatory in this deal, it’s believed that she served as a “white glove,” a person who operates on behalf of another to conceal their identity — but it remains unclear if this was for Shanghai Hexi and Kang Wei or some other third party. There is not much information on Alice Huang’s activities between 2019 and 2021. However, Shanghai Hexi invested in Shanghai Longjing Information Technology, a data center-focused subsidiary of Century Huatong in 2020, where Ms. Huang served as a director between 2021 and 2022, according to a report by The Wire China . At about the same time, 7Road Holdings expanded into cloud computing, just before ChatGPT brought AI LLMs to the forefront. The U.S. government’s ban on the export of Nvidia chips to China put this investment in jeopardy, though, forcing it to spin off the business as 7Road International in Singapore. We don’t know when 7Road Holdings sold its Singapore subsidiary, but corporate records show that by the time the company was renamed Megaspeed in March 2023, it was already under the ownership of Huang Le Limited and led by Ms. Huang. It was sold again in November 2023 to Swiftdata, a company owned by Singaporean Tan Yong Pong. Axios said that she left the firm as a managing director soon after this acquisition, but sources said that she kept working with the company afterward, with Kang Wei helping her get it off the ground. In the same year, Shanghai Century Litong was founded to build AI data centers in Shanghai and Shenzhen, with Jiangsu Lettall Electronic Co., an electronic components manufacturer, holding a 90% stake, while the remaining 10% is owned by Century Longteng, as reported by BigGo Finance . It should be noted that Century Longteng was renamed from Shanghai Yuxi Investment Management, with the firm pivoting its business from finance to cloud computing, and that even though Alice Huang has already exited the company by this time, it’s under the control of Huang Yu, who some sources say is Ms. Huang’s sister. A year after these data center acquisitions, Alice Huang began to be spotted in public with the former Nvidia CEO. A LinkedIn post showed her having drinks with a leather-clad Jensen Huang alongside other tech executives from NetThunder and Gigabyte at a post-Computex 2024 event. She was once again seen having dinner with him in a Taipei restaurant as reporters tried to interview him while one kid demanded his attention off camera. But more than these public sightings, Alice herself boasted about her “closeness” to the then CEO. People close to her said that she regularly posted photos with Jensen on her WeChat account, and even shared others with potential customers to help establish her credibility. She even reportedly claimed that Mr. Huang would celebrate her birthdays with restaurant dinners and gifts, with one Nvidia China sales employee also saying that she was a familiar face at the company’s annual event for China partners. An investigation revealed that from 2023 to 2025, Megaspeed imported $4.6 billion worth of Nvidia AI chips, while another $2 billion was routed through Speedmatrix , Megaspeed’s subsidiary with offices in Johor, Malaysia. Shanghai Century Litong also reportedly bought AI GPUs from other sources, with estimates putting the total number of banned chips moved through Alice Huang’s assistance at around 240,000, putting the shipments’ worth at around $7.5 billion. But even as Ms. Huang was making her international moves, Kang Wei was facing trouble at home. Chinese regulators fined him 2.5 million yuan, or approximately $380,000, in 2025, for violating sections of China’s Securities Law. This also led to a warning letter against him, issued in August 2026 by the China Securities Regulatory Commission. Despite running into trouble with the authorities, this massive paper trail showed how Kang Wei actively made moves that put Alice Huang close to Jensen Huang. Some questions remain, though, about the U.S. intelligence community’s claims that she worked with the Ministry of State Security (MSS), China’s primary intelligence and counterintelligence agency. If it’s true that Alice Huang worked with the MSS and passed on information to the agency, did she specifically target Jensen Huang, or did the spy agency simply discover their indiscretion and use that to force her to cooperate? Was all this planned by the MSS, or were they just shrewd business moves that allowed Kang to make more money while going under the radar of regulators? These are questions that only Kang Wei and Alice Huang (or the Chinese spy agency) can answer. But no matter the case, the fact remains that China acquired advanced AI chips that were supposed to be out of its reach because of this couple’s connections.

# Securing the Asia-Pacific digital battlespace: TechNet Indo-Pacific 2026

From electronic warfare threats to coalition data sharing, discover how US and allied forces are strengthening the digital battlespace across the Indo-Pacific.

By [Breaking Defense](https://breakingdefense.com/author/breakingdefense/) on November 13, 2026 5:27 pm

At AFCEA’s TechNet Indo-Pacific 2026, senior military leaders and defense experts outlined the challenges facing US and allied forces, from persistent electronic warfare threats on the Korean Peninsula to the evolving Taiwan conflict timeline and the need for stronger regional data-sharing capabilities.

title: What Jensen Huang’s Nvidia exit means for Washington, Wall Street, and Beijing
zh_title: 黄仁勋退出英伟达对华盛顿、华尔街和北京意味着什么
summary: 黄仁勋退出 Nvidia 对华盛顿、华尔街和北京意味着什么 - 大西洋理事会东亚科技与创新美国和加拿大 黄仁勋退出 Nvidia 对华盛顿、华尔街和北京意味着什么 有很多事情需要处理。周四，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋因婚外情报道而辞职，其中包括与一名疑似中国间谍的婚外情。但其影响超出了该人和他的前公司的范围，该公司因其领先的计算机处理器而成为人工智能（AI）繁荣的关键引擎。下面，大西洋理事会的专家们
content:
黄仁勋退出英伟达对华盛顿、华尔街和北京意味着什么 - 大西洋理事会
东亚科技与创新美国和加拿大
黄仁勋退出英伟达对华盛顿、华尔街和北京意味着什么
有很多事情需要处理。周四，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋因婚外情报道而辞职，其中包括与一名疑似中国间谍的婚外情。但其影响超出了该人和他的前公司的范围，该公司因其领先的计算机处理器而成为人工智能（AI）繁荣的关键引擎。下面，大西洋理事会专家将探讨人事变动将如何影响美国政策、全球市场等。
今天为您带来的专家反应
Trisha Ray：地质技术中心副主任兼常驻研究员
Graham Brookie (@GrahamBrookie)：技术项目和战略副总裁
Jessie Yin：地缘经济中心副主任
Kenton Thibaut (@kentonthibaut)：数字取证研究实验室中国高级研究员
Trisha 解释道，英伟达的先进芯片是“美国减缓对手人工智能能力的关键”。但这种优势也是“单点故障”，因为美国的出口管制力度取决于少数公司及其内部人员的安全措施。
格雷厄姆认为，这一事件并不是美国情报部门的失败，“而是美国政府在管理国家安全威胁方面协调和政策执行方面的更广泛的失败”。由于人工智能行业容易受到知识产权盗窃和直接攻击，华盛顿在风险管理和出口政策执行方面“措手不及”。
“对于投资者来说，将英伟达的成功与黄仁勋分开是很困难的，而对于华盛顿来说，将英伟达与国家安全分开也几乎同样困难，”杰西说。她现在认为国会有机会对该公司对国家安全的影响进行更大的监督，并加强半导体出口管制。肯顿指出，国会对芯片限制的势头不断增强，例如《人工智能监督法案》、《芯片安全法案》和《匹配法案》。
展望未来，特丽莎敦促政府加强审查。她认为，“鉴于支持美国人工智能领先地位的公司很少，政策制定者应该认真考虑政府的直接监督”，例如对公司领导层及其主要客户的安全许可要求，以及对出口实体的安全审计作为出口许可证的先决条件。
由于英伟达股价下跌，今天市场小幅下跌。黄仁勋的离开让投资者怀疑，如果没有这位已成为其成功代名词的领导者，英伟达能否维持其主导地位。杰西推测，公司“将在一段时间内不稳定”。
这些股份比英伟达的股价还要高。格雷厄姆警告说，美国经济已经高度依赖于少数人工智能公司的命运，这些公司“也恰好是该国在地缘政治竞争的决定性领域中的主要战略资产”。其中一个失败可能会影响整个美国经济和国家安全生态系统。
除了销售芯片之外，英伟达还成为人工智能热潮的主要融资者——被称为“人工智能中央银行”——投资初创企业并为购买其产品的客户提供支持。杰西表示，未来几个月将展示“英伟达对人工智能需求本身的整合程度如何”。

What Jensen Huang’s Nvidia exit means for Washington, Wall Street, and Beijing
It’s a lot to process. On Thursday, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. But the implications extend beyond the man and his former company, a critical engine of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom because of its leading-edge computer processors. Below, Atlantic Council experts work through how the personnel shakeup could impact US policy, global markets, and more.
TODAY’S EXPERT REACTION BROUGHT TO YOU BY
Trisha Ray: Associate director and resident fellow at the GeoTech Center
Graham Brookie (@GrahamBrookie): Vice president for technology programs and strategy
Jessie Yin: Associate director with the GeoEconomics Center
Kenton Thibaut (@kentonthibaut): Senior resident China fellow at the Digital Forensic Research Lab
Nvidia’s advanced chips are “the linchpin of the United States’ leverage in slowing down the AI capabilities of its adversaries,” Trisha explains. But that advantage is also “a single point of failure,” since US export controls are only as strong as the security practices of a handful of companies and people within them.
Graham sees the incident not as a failure in US intelligence, “but rather a broader failure of coordination and policy execution in how the US government manages national security threats.” With the AI industry vulnerable to intellectual property theft and direct targeting, Washington was “caught flat footed” in risk management and export policy enforcement.
“As difficult as it is for investors to separate Nvidia’s success from Jensen Huang, it has become nearly as difficult for Washington to separate Nvidia from national security,” Jessie argues. She now sees an opening for Congress to exert greater oversight of the company’s impact on national security and tighten semiconductor export controls. Kenton points to growing momentum in Congress behind chip restrictions such as the AI Overwatch Act, the Chip Security Act, and the MATCH Act.
Going forward, Trisha urges greater government scrutiny. “Given how few companies underpin the US AI lead, policymakers should seriously consider direct government oversight,” she argues, such as security clearance–like requirements for company leadership and their major customers, as well as security audits of the exporting entities as a precondition for export licenses.
Markets were down slightly today, as Nvidia shares took a hit. Huang’s departure has investors wondering if Nvidia can sustain its dominance without the leader who became a synonym to its success. The company is “going to be unsteady for a while,” Jessie surmises.
The stakes are higher than Nvidia’s stock price alone. The US economy is already highly exposed to the fortunes of a handful of AI companies that “also happen to be the country’s primary strategic assets in a determinative domain of geopolitical competition,” Graham warns. A failure at one could reverberate across the US economy and national security ecosystem.
Beyond selling chips, Nvidia has become a major financier of the AI boom—known as “the central bank of AI”—investing in startups and supporting customers that buy its products. Jessie says that the coming months will show “how integral Nvidia has become to AI demand itself.”
Sign up to receive rapid insight in your inbox from Atlantic Council experts on global events as they unfold.
Ahead of a planned meeting next week between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, Beijing warned Washington earlier today against further technology restrictions, Kenton notes.
Huang had long opposed strict export controls and was able to speak with both Trump and Xi. “But with Huang out of the picture, there is potentially more political leeway to push forward on a more hawkish approach,” Kenton says.
Jessie adds that the scandal has “permanently damaged the company’s credibility to push back on export controls,” relationships aside.
But tougher controls could invite retaliation, Kenton warns. “Beijing could answer new restrictions with curbs on critical minerals or probes of other American firms,” potentially complicating the upcoming Trump-Xi meeting.

summary: 阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰“迈克尔·墨菲”号 (DDG 112) 搭载直升机海上打击中队 (HSM) 第 71 分遣队，在美国第 3、第 7 和第 5 舰队作战区域部署了 11 个月后返回其夏威夷珍珠港-希卡姆联合基地的母港，特别是在史诗狂怒行动期间的持续战斗行动， 11 月 12 日。迈克尔·墨菲于 2025 年 12 月 1 日离开珍珠港，作为第 21 驱逐舰中队 (DESRON) 下的第 3 航母战斗群 (CSG) 3 的一部分，与旗舰尼米兹级航空母舰亚伯拉罕·林肯号一起作战
content:
阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰“迈克尔·墨菲”号 (DDG 112) 搭载直升机海上打击中队 (HSM) 第 71 分遣队，在美国第 3、第 7 和第 5 舰队作战区域部署了 11 个月后返回其夏威夷珍珠港-希卡姆联合基地的母港，特别是在史诗狂怒行动期间的持续战斗行动， 11 月 12 日。

迈克尔·墨菲号于 2025 年 12 月 1 日离开珍珠港，作为第 21 驱逐舰中队 (DESRON) 下的第 3 航母战斗群 (CSG) 3 的一部分，与旗舰尼米兹级航空母舰亚伯拉罕·林肯号 (CVN 72)、阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰斯普鲁恩斯号 (DDG 111) 和小弗兰克·彼得森号 (DDG) 一起行动121）和舰载机联队（CVW）9。

迈克尔·墨菲号于 2026 年 1 月下旬进入美国中央司令部责任区，该舰在史诗愤怒行动的前线服役。

为了表彰迈克尔·墨菲号航空母舰及其船员在执行数十次战斧对地攻击巡航导弹袭击以及防御敌方无人机和导弹攻击时所表现出的非凡英雄主义和战斗成就，被授予总统集体奖章（PUC）和战斗行动绶带（CAR）。
“迈克尔·墨菲号的水手们在这次部署中表现出了无与伦比的勇气、专业精神和卓越的作战能力，”海军中校说。大卫·尼古拉斯，迈克尔·墨菲的指挥官。 “无论是击败来袭的空中和地面威胁，还是通过有争议的咽喉要道领导行动，这支部队都毫不犹豫。他们响应了我们国家的每一个召唤，保卫了我们的盟友，不辜负英雄的同名。我为这支部队感到无比自豪。”

在整个部署过程中，迈克尔·墨菲在北阿拉伯海、阿曼湾和霍尔木兹海峡执行 60 年来首次海上封锁中发挥了重要作用。作为第 50 特遣部队 (TF-50) 水面行动小组指挥官，迈克尔·墨菲指挥并协调了 14 艘联军和美国船只的防御，包括驱逐舰、濒海战斗舰、六艘美国海岸警卫队快速反应快艇和后勤舰队加油船。该船在水面、空中和水雷攻击的威胁下完成了 12 次有争议地通过霍尔木兹海峡，护送四艘商船到达安全地带。
在为期 11 个月的部署过程中，迈克尔·墨菲仍然留在战区，并继续在 TF-50 的领导下与 CSG-10 和 CSG-5 的参谋人员、舰艇和飞机一起行动。该舰航行了超过 97,000 海里，进行了 43 次海上补给和 8 次战斗港口加油，运输了超过 800 万加仑的 F-76 船用柴油和 200 万加仑的 JP-5 喷气燃料。该舰在战斗条件下安全接收了 1,100 托盘食品、物资、维修零件和邮件。

直升机海上打击中队（HSM）第71第2支队飞行330架次，无事故飞行900多个小时，其中战斗飞行273.4小时。

在美国第七舰队服役期间，迈克尔·墨菲在南中国海和菲律宾海开展了战区水面和反潜行动，为盟友提供了保障，并对我们的对手提供了威慑。

作为美国太平洋舰队的一个组成部分，美国第三舰队领导该地区的海军部队，并提供必要的现实、相关的训练，以在从作战行动到人道主义援助和救灾等全方位的军事行动中履行我们海军的职责

【原文 English Original】
Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Michael Murphy (DDG 112), with embarked Helicopter Maritime Strike Squadron (HSM) 71 Detachment 2, returned to its homeport of Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam, Hawaii following an 11-month deployment to the U.S. 3rd, 7th, and 5th Fleet areas of operations, highlighted by sustained combat actions during Operation Epic Fury, Nov. 12.

Michael Murphy departed Pearl Harbor Dec. 1, 2025, operating as part of Carrier Strike Group 3 (CSG) 3 under Destroyer Squadron (DESRON) 21, operating alongside flagship Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN 72), Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyers USS Spruance (DDG 111) and USS Frank E. Petersen Jr. (DDG 121), and Carrier Air Wing (CVW) 9.

Michael Murphy entered the U.S. Central Command area of responsibility in late January 2026, where the warship served on the front lines of Operation Epic Fury.

In recognition of extraordinary heroism and combat achievement while executing dozens of Tomahawk land-attack cruise missile strikes and defending against hostile drone and missile attacks, USS Michael Murphy and its crew were awarded the Presidential Unit Citation (PUC) and the Combat Action Ribbon (CAR).

“The Sailors of Michael Murphy demonstrated unmatched grit, professionalism, and warfighting excellence during this deployment,” said Cmdr. David Nicolas, commanding officer of Michael Murphy. “Whether defeating incoming air and surface threats or leading operations through contested choke points, this crew never hesitated. They answered every call of our nation, defended our allies, and lived up to the heroic namesake. I could not be prouder of this crew.”

Throughout the deployment, Michael Murphy played an essential role in enforcing the first naval blockade in 60 years, operating in the North Arabian Sea, Gulf of Oman, and Strait of Hormuz. Serving as Surface Action Group Commander for Task Force 50 (TF-50), Michael Murphy commanded and coordinated the defense of 14 coalition and U.S. vessels, including destroyers, Littoral Combat Ships, six U.S. Coast Guard Fast Response Cutters, and logistics fleet oilers. The ship completed 12 contested transits of the Strait of Hormuz under threat of surface, air, and mine attack, escorting four merchant tankers to safety.

Over the course of the 11-month deployment Michael Murphy remained in theater and continued to operate under TF-50 leadership, alongside the staffs, ships, and aircraft of CSG-10 and CSG-5. The warship steamed more than 97,000 nautical miles, conducted 43 replenishments-at-sea and eight combat in-port refuelings, transferring over 8 million gallons of F-76 marine diesel fuel and 2 million gallons of JP-5 jet fuel. The ship safely received 1,100 pallets of food, stores, repair parts, and mail under combat conditions.

The air detachment of Helicopter Maritime Strike Squadron (HSM) 71 Detachment 2 flew 330 sorties and over 900 mishap-free flight hours, including 273.4 combat flight hours.

While operating in U.S. 7th Fleet, Michael Murphy conducted theater surface and anti-submarine operations in the South China and Philippine Seas, assuring allies and providing deterrence to our adversaries.

An integral part of the U.S. Pacific Fleet, U.S. 3rd Fleet leads naval forces in the region and provides the realistic, relevant training necessary to execute our Navy's role across the full spectrum of military operations – from combat operations to humanitarian assistance and disaster response. U.S. 3rd Fleet works together with allies and partners to advance freedom of navigation and overflight, the rule of law, and other principles that underpin security for the region.

For more news from U.S. 3rd Fleet, visit [https://www.dvidshub.net/unit/COM-US3rdFleet](https://www.dvidshub.net/unit/COM-US3rdFleet).

For more information on Carrier Strike Group 3 and Michael Murphy’s deployment, please visit [https://www.dvidshub.net/feature/ABECSG](https://www.dvidshub.net/feature/ABECSG) or Michael Murphy’s unit page at [https://www.dvidshub.net/unit/DDG112](https://www.dvidshub.net/unit/DDG112).

title: Launch Preview: Starship, Vulcan, and Electron launches scheduled for busy week
zh_title: 发射预览：Starship、Vulcan 和 Electron 计划在繁忙的一周发射
summary: 来自四个国家的七枚火箭将于本周发射。星际飞船将尝试其迄今为止最重要的任务，而猎鹰 9 号将为美国太空军发射一对机密有效载荷。联合发射联盟计划让 Vulcan 执行其返回飞行任务，而 Electron 则将完成第 100 次任务，具有里程碑意义。在国际上，中国和韩国将分别发射未知的有效载荷和演示任务。猎鹰 9 号 | USSF-627（“R-5”）本周首次发射将由猎鹰 9 号火箭提供机密有效载荷
content:
来自四个国家的七枚火箭将于本周发射。星际飞船将尝试其迄今为止最重要的任务，而猎鹰 9 号将为美国太空军发射一对机密有效载荷。联合发射联盟计划让 Vulcan 执行其返回飞行任务，而 Electron 则将完成第 100 次任务，具有里程碑意义。在国际上，中国和韩国将分别发射未知的有效载荷和演示任务。猎鹰 9 号 | USSF-627（“R-5”）本周首次发射将由猎鹰 9 号火箭为美国太空军 (USSF) 提供机密有效载荷。该任务被指定为 USSF-627，最初计划于 11 月 8 日星期日发射。猎鹰 9 号现定于太平洋标准时间 11 月 9 日星期一晚上 7:07（世界标准时间 10 月 10 日 03:07）从范登堡太空部队基地 (VSFB) 的 4 号东部太空发射综合体 (SLC-4E) 起飞，距太平洋标准时间晚上 11:03 (07:03) 的窗口期已过去四分钟。 UTC 时间 11 月 10 日）。由于有效载荷的机密性质，卫星的确切数量尚不清楚。一些指标表明，基于猎鹰 9 号第二级的降落区，星盾将进行发射。 Starshield是为美国政府打造的Starlink版本，其主要客户是USSF、国家侦察办公室和太空发展局。范登堡太空部队基地 4E 号航天发射场发射台上的猎鹰 9 号火箭。
（图片来源：SpaceX）Falcon 9 是一款两级、70 m 高、部分可重复使用的火箭，第一级使用九个 Merlin 1D 海平面发动机，第二级使用单个真空优化的 Merlin 1D。Falcon 9 的第一级降落在自主无人机船上或着陆点，其整流罩在飞行后回收并重复使用。两个阶段都使用液体煤油和液氧作为推进剂。助推器 B1103 将在其第七次飞行中支持这项任务。此前，该助推器已支持 NROL-179、第一批传输层 A 和 E 以及三个星链任务的发射。猎鹰 9 号将搭乘 SpaceX 的无人机“当然我仍然爱你”着陆。米尔 |演示飞行 11 月 10 日星期二，韩国计划发射韩国军方小型卫星运载火箭和平号的第二次飞行。继 2023 年 12 月进行了不包括第二级的试飞之后，此次发射将是全尺寸火箭的首次轨道飞行。启动窗口于 05:00 UTC 开始，并延长至 09:00 UTC。和平号是一款四级固体燃料运载火箭，第四级采用液体燃料，可实现精确入轨。 2023 年 12 月飞行的版本能够运载 700 公斤至近地轨道，该版本疑似能够运载 1,000 公斤左右。长征2D |有效载荷未知 11 月 11 日星期三，长征 2D (CZ-2D) 火箭计划从酒泉卫星发射中心发射升空。
目前，发射计划于 11:40 UTC 进行，距离 11:32 UTC 开启并持续到 12:05 UTC 的窗口还有 8 分钟的时间。CZ-2D 将向轨道发射未知有效载荷。 CZ-2D 是一款两级、41 米高的运载火箭，能够向近地轨道 (LEO) 发射 3,500 公斤的重量。 CZ-2D的第一级和第二级均由四氧化二氮和不对称二甲肼提供动力，这两种推进剂都是自燃推进剂。周三的发射将是长征二号丁的第 107 次发射，也是 2026 年的第六次发射。快舟 11 |有效载荷未知本周第二个也是最后一个预定的中国任务

【原文 English Original】
Seven rockets from four countries are set to launch this week. Starship is set to attempt its most consequential mission yet, while Falcon 9 is set to launch a pair of classified payloads for the United States Space Force. The United Launch Alliance is scheduled to fly Vulcan on its return-to-flight mission, and Electron is set to reach a milestone 100th mission. Internationally, China and South Korea are set to launch an unknown payload and a demonstration mission, respectively. Falcon 9 | USSF-627 (“R-5”) The first launch of the week will feature Falcon 9 delivering a classified payload for the United States Space Force (USSF). The mission, designated USSF-627, was initially scheduled to launch on Sunday, Nov. 8. Falcon 9 is now set to take off from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) on Monday, Nov. 9, at 7:07 PM PST (03:07 UTC on Nov. 10), four minutes into a window that extends until 11:03 PM PST (07:03 UTC on Nov. 10). Due to the classified nature of the payload, the exact quantity of satellites is unknown. Some indicators suggest a Starshield launch, based on drop zones for Falcon 9’s second stage. Starshield is a version of Starlink built for the United States government, with its primary customers being the USSF, National Reconnaissance Office, and the Space Development Agency. A Falcon 9 on the launch pad at Space Launch Complex-4E on Vandenberg Space Force Base. (Credit: SpaceX) Falcon 9 is a two-stage, 70 m-tall, partially reusable rocket that uses nine Merlin 1D sea-level engines on its first stage and a single vacuum-optimized Merlin 1D on its second stage. Falcon 9’s first stage lands either aboard an autonomous droneship or at a landing site, with its fairings being recovered and reused after flight. Both stages utilize liquid kerosene and liquid oxygen as propellants. Booster B1103 will be supporting this mission on its seventh flight. Previously, this booster has supported the launches of NROL-179, Tranche 1 Transport Layers A and E, and three Starlink missions. Falcon 9 will land downrange aboard SpaceX’s droneship Of Course I Still Love You . Mir | Demo Flight On Tuesday, Nov. 10, South Korea is set to launch the second flight of Mir, the South Korean military’s small satellite launch vehicle. This launch is set to be the first orbital flight of the full-scale rocket, following a test flight in December 2023 that did not include the second stage. The launch window opens at 05:00 UTC and extends until 09:00 UTC. Mir is a four-stage, solid-fuel launch vehicle with a liquid-fueled fourth stage for precise orbital insertion. The version that flew in December 2023 was capable of 700 kg to LEO, with this version suspected to be capable of around 1,000 kg. Chang Zheng 2D | Unknown Payload On Wednesday, Nov. 11, a Chang Zheng 2D (CZ-2D) rocket is scheduled to launch out of the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center. The launch is currently scheduled for 11:40 UTC, eight minutes into a window that opens at 11:32 UTC and extends until 12:05 UTC. CZ-2D will deliver an unknown payload into orbit. CZ-2D is a two-stage, 41 m-tall launch vehicle capable of delivering 3,500 kg to low-Earth orbit (LEO). CZ-2D’s first and second stages are both powered by dinitrogen tetroxide and unsymmetrical dimethyl hydrazine, both hypergolic propellants. Wednesday’s launch will be the 107th overall for CZ-2D, and sixth in 2026. Kuaizhou 11 | Unknown Payload The second and final scheduled Chinese mission of the week will see a Kuaizhou 11 rocket launch on Thursday, Nov. 12. Liftoff is set for 19:50 UTC from Site 95A at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, during a 45-minute launch window. Kuaizhou 11 is a four-stage Chinese rocket manufactured by the China Aerospace Science and Industry Corporation. Standing 25.3 m tall, the rocket can loft 1,500 kg to LEO with a liftoff thrust of 1,250 kN. This mission will be the eighth overall Kuaizhou 11 mission and the fourth of 2026. Vulcan VC6L | Amazon Leo (LV-01) United Launch Alliance’s (ULA) Vulcan rocket is set to launch on Friday, Nov. 13, from Space Launch Complex 41 (SLC-41) at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. The 30-minute launch window opens at 12:54 PM EST (17:54 UTC). This will be the first flight of Vulcan in over nine months, following the ejection of one of Vulcan’s GEM-63XL solid rocket boosters at T+69 seconds on the USSF-87 mission. Flying aboard Vulcan will be a stack of 40 Amazon Leo satellites for Amazon’s Leo satellite internet constellation, a rival to SpaceX’s Starlink. A ULA Vulcan (USSF-87) sits next to a SpaceX Crew Dragon (Crew-12). (Credit: Tyler Gray for NSF) Vulcan is a two-stage launch vehicle with a range of launch configurations. Vulcan’s first stage is powered by two BE-4 engines built by Blue Origin, running on liquid methane and liquid oxygen propellants. Its second stage, Centaur V, is powered by twin RL10C engines running on liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen. Centaur V can be configured as Centaur LEO, High Energy, or Endurance. Vulcan can also be configured with solid rocket boosters to augment liftoff thrust, with options ranging from zero to two, four, or six boosters. The payload is encapsulated by either a short (15.5 m) or a long (21.3 m) fairing. Vulcan will debut the Vulcan VC6L variant, designated by six solid boosters and the long fairing option. Vulcan will debut the LEO-optimized Centaur V, which is 1.94 m smaller than the existing Centaur V High Energy, which has flown on all previous Vulcan launches. Additionally, this flight is a certification flight of this Vulcan configuration for the United States Space Force. Amazon Leo (LV-01) will be the first of 38 scheduled for Vulcan and the fifth overall mission for Vulcan. Starship | Flight 15 / Starlink Group 31-2 Pending regulatory approval, Starship is set to fly its next, and most significant, mission no earlier than Friday, Nov. 13, at 4:45 PM CST (22:45 UTC). The launch window extends until 6:00 PM CST (00:00 UTC on Nov. 14). Flight 15 will feature two notable events: the first booster-catch attempt since Flight 8, following stage separation, and the first attempt to catch the ship, roughly 22 hours after liftoff. Starship is a two-stage, super-heavy-lift launch vehicle capable of lofting an estimated 100 tonnes. The first stage, named Super Heavy, features 33 Raptor 3 engines, running off of liquid methane and liquid oxygen propellants. The second stage, named Starship, features six Raptor 3 engines, three sea-level and three vacuum-optimized, also running off of liquid methane and liquid oxygen. Flying on Flight 15 will be Ship 42 and Booster 22, both on their first flights. Flight 15 is expected to deliver 26 Starlink v3 satellites to LEO. Like Flight 14, three of these satellites will feature imaging capabilities for imaging the heat shield of Starship in orbit. Flight 15 will be the 15th full-stack launch of Starship and the fourth for the system’s V3 configuration. Falcon 9 | USSF-317 (“R-6”) Falcon 9 is set to fly again on Friday, Nov. 13, from VSFB with another USSF mission. The designation for this flight is USSF-317. The launch window opens at 8:09 PM PST (04:09 UTC on Nov. 14), and lasts for four hours. This mission will fly another unknown quantity of presumed Starshield satellites to LEO. Booster B1100 will support this mission, marking its 11th flight. This booster has previously supported NROL-105, USSF-385, and eight Starlink missions. B1100 will land downrange aboard SpaceX’s droneship Of Course I Still Love You . Electron during its 95th launch “Happily Ever Faster.” Credit: Rocket Lab) Electron | The Mountain God Rises The last scheduled launch of the week will see Rocket Lab’s Electron launch from the Mahia Peninsula in New Zealand on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 05:30 UTC. This flight of Electron, named “The Mountain God Rises,” will deliver another iQPS satellite into LEO for iQPS’s synthetic aperture radar constellation (SAR). SAR is used to image the surface of the Earth and can penetrate through cloud layers. Electron is a two-stage small-lift vehicle capable of delivering up to 300 kg to LEO and 200 kg to Sun-synchronous orbit. The vehicle is fueled by liquid kerosene and liquid oxygen, which powers nine Rutherford engines on the first stage and a single vacuum-optimized Rutherford on the second stage. This mission will serve as Electron’s 100th overall mission — a notable milestone for the small rocket that first flew in 2017. In addition, this mission will serve as the 269th orbital launch attempt worldwide in 2026. ( Lead Image: Falcon 9 launches from Florida. Credit: Julia Bergeron for NSF) The post Launch Preview: Starship, Vulcan, and Electron launches scheduled for busy week appeared first on NASASpaceFlight.com .

title: USS City of Bismarck Welcomes New Military Crew Commander

summary: 2026 年 11 月 13 日，日本横须贺——由军事海运司令部运营的远征快速运输舰俾斯麦市号 (EPF 9) 迎来了新任指挥官，中校。蒂亚·迈尔斯在横须贺舰队活动船上举行的仪式上。迈尔斯从中校手中接过指挥权。 VanAnh McCormick，在将该船移交给 MILCREW II 之前担任军事船员 I 的指挥官。 “从我们的人员流动开始，我们不再是 MILCREW II 和 CIVMAR；我们都是俾斯麦市号航空母舰，”迈尔斯在向由水手和公务员组成的混合船员发表的讲话中说道。 “这就是全部
content:
2026 年 11 月 13 日

日本横须贺——

由军事海运司令部运营的远征快速运输舰俾斯麦市号（EPF 9）迎来了新任指挥官，中校。蒂亚·迈尔斯在横须贺舰队活动船上举行的仪式上。迈尔斯从中校手中接过指挥权。 VanAnh McCormick，在将该船移交给 MILCREW II 之前担任军事船员 I 的指挥官。

“从我们的人员流动开始，我们不再是 MILCREW II 和 CIVMAR；我们都是俾斯麦市号航空母舰，”迈尔斯在向由水手和公务员组成的混合船员发表的讲话中说道。 “‘保持媒体报道’是我们的全部工作！我们必须在场并准备好参与，同时互相支持，以确保我们的成功。Crew I 奠定了基础，我们的工作就是在此基础上继续发展。Possumus Efficiemus：我们可以而且我们将会实现。”

迈尔斯是南卡罗来纳州哥伦比亚人，2014 年从弗朗西斯马里恩大学毕业并获得数学学士学位后，被任命为海军军官。她还拥有海军研究生院的高级工商管理硕士学位。

在海上，迈尔斯曾在阿利伯克号航空母舰 (DDG 51)、珍珠港号航空母舰 (LSD 52) 和哈珀斯渡口号航空母舰 (LSD 49) 上服役。
在岸上，她在圣地亚哥海军水面和水雷作战发展中心和水面高级作战学校担任两栖作战战术教员。迈尔斯接替了麦考密克，麦考密克于 2026 年 7 月接管了 MILCREW I 的指挥权，并带领船员完成了有史以来的首次 EPF 部署。部署期间，船员航行超过4000海里，访问了4个海外港口。机组人员为“锐剑”演习提供了后勤保障，并完成了任务要求的所有准备工作。此外，供应部门还入围了 David M. Cook 食品服务卓越奖的决赛。

俾斯麦号是EPF级第九艘舰艇。这些浅吃水、全铝制商用双体船旨在以 35 节的平均速度将 600 短吨军用货物运输 1,200 海里。该船设有用于直升机操作的飞行甲板、车辆卸载坡道部署以及增强沿海操作和港口通道的浅吃水。这些能力使 EPF 能够在严峻或受损的港口提供灵活的物流支持、快速运输和救灾。

该船的船员由军事人员和文职海员组成。 MILCREW 轮流部署，基地设在圣地亚哥，而该舰的母港是横须贺，由美国第七舰队负责作战控制。
军事海运司令部负责指挥和支持大约 140 艘民用船只的行动，这些船只为美国海军舰船补充海上补给、执行专门任务、在全球范围内预置战斗货物、提供支持服务以及向部署的美国部队运输军事装备和补给品。

【原文 English Original】
13 November 2026

YOKOSUKA, Japan --

The expeditionary fast transport USS City of Bismarck (EPF 9), operated by Military Sealift Command, welcomed its new commanding officer, Lt. Cmdr. Tia Myers, during a ceremony aboard the ship at Fleet Activities Yokosuka. Myers assumed command from Lt. Cmdr. VanAnh McCormick, who served as the Military Crew I commander before turning the ship over to MILCREW II.

“Starting with our turnover, we are no longer MILCREW II and CIVMARs; we are all USS City of Bismarck,” Myers said in her address to the hybrid crew of sailors and civil service mariners. “It is all of our job to ‘keep the press!’ We have to be present and ready to engage while supporting each other to ensure our success. Crew I laid the foundation, and it is our job to build upon it. Possumus Efficiemus: We can and we will accomplish.”

A native of Columbia, South Carolina, Myers commissioned as a naval officer in 2014 after graduating from Francis Marion University with a bachelor’s degree in mathematics. She also holds an executive master’s degree in business administration from the Naval Postgraduate School.

At sea, Myers served aboard USS Arleigh Burke (DDG 51), USS Pearl Harbor (LSD 52) and USS Harpers Ferry (LSD 49).

Ashore, she served as an amphibious warfare tactics instructor at the Naval Surface and Mine Warfighting Development Center and Surface Advanced Warfighting School in San Diego. Myers relieved McCormick, who took command of MILCREW I in July 2026 and led the crew through its first ever EPF deployment. During the deployment, the crew sailed more than 4,000 nautical miles and visited four overseas ports. The crew provided logistics support for Exercise Keen Sword and completed all ready for tasking requirements. In addition, the supply department became a finalist for the David M. Cook Food Service Excellence Award.

Bismarck is the ninth ship in the EPF class. These shallow-draft, all-aluminum, commercial-based catamarans are designed to transport 600 short tons of military cargo 1,200 nautical miles at an average speed of 35 knots. The ship features a flight deck for helicopter operations, a vehicle offload ramp deployment, and a shallow draft that enhances littoral operations and port access. These capabilities allow the EPF to deliver flexible logistics support, rapid transport and disaster relief in austere or damaged ports.

The ship operates with a hybrid crew of military personnel and civil service mariners. The MILCREWs rotate for deployments and are based in San Diego, while the ship is homeported in Yokosuka under the operational control of U.S. 7th Fleet.

Military Sealift Command directs and supports operations for approximately 140 civilian-crewed ships that replenish U.S. Navy ships at sea, conduct specialized missions, preposition combat cargo worldwide, provide support services, and transport military equipment and supplies to deployed U.S. forces.

title: Elon Musk says it ‘would be an honor’ to hire ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
zh_title: 埃隆·马斯克表示，能够聘请被罢免的英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋“将是一种荣幸”
summary: 黄仁勋在情报来源披露他与一名疑似中国间谍的关系两周后，以及他与英伟达副总裁的恋情曝光一天后，辞去了英伟达首席执行官的职务。但在此举之前几个小时，当有传言称 Nvidia 董事会计划将他驱逐时，埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 就已经表示愿意聘用这位 Nvidia 前首席执行官。一位随机的 X 用户发帖称，“埃隆请雇用詹森”，这位亿万富翁回答道：“那将是一种荣幸。” @zerohedge 这将是一种荣幸 2026 年 11 月 12 日，尽管詹森有丑闻
content:
黄仁勋在情报来源披露他与一名疑似中国间谍的关系两周后，以及他与英伟达副总裁的恋情曝光一天后，辞去了英伟达首席执行官的职务。但在此举之前几个小时，当有传言称 Nvidia 董事会计划将他驱逐时，埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 就已经表示愿意聘用这位 Nvidia 前首席执行官。一位随机的 X 用户发帖称，“埃隆请雇用詹森”，这位亿万富翁回答道：“那将是一种荣幸。” @zerohedge 这将是一种荣誉，2026 年 11 月 12 日 尽管 Jensen 目前面临丑闻，但他仍然拥有工程专业知识、对行业及其内部运作的深入了解，再加上在世界各地的多重联系，这对于任何想要进入半导体行业的公司来说都是极其有价值的。这正是埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 在他的 Terafab 项目中所做的事情，他于 2025 年 11 月首次提到该项目。黄仁勋甚至警告说，这将是一个挑战，并指出“台积电谋生的工程、科学和艺术是极其困难的。”尽管如此，马斯克仍将资源投入到该项目中，Terafab 工厂的建设正如火如荼地进行，并计划在 2028 年下半年实现芯片量产。马斯克本人表示，该工厂的目标是到 2032 年实现每月 100 万片晶圆的产能。
特斯拉有着雄心勃勃的人工智能加速器路线图，SpaceX甚至宣称在未来制造自己的GPU。我们仍然不知道黄仁勋的计划是什么，但尽管他不再是英伟达董事会及其领导层的成员，詹森和他的妻子洛里仍然通过各种信托和有限责任公司共同持有约8亿股英伟达股票，而黄仁勋本人则拥有约7000万股英伟达股票。除此之外，他仍然收到国会发出的讨论英伟达安全协议的邀请，如果他拒绝的话，这可能会变成传票，尽管我们不知道他的辞职会对闭门会议产生什么影响。据报道，FBI 正在调查他与 Megaspeed 高管 Alice Huang 的关系，后者据称在向中国进口价值 75 亿美元的 Nvidia AI GPU 过程中发挥了重要作用，并涉嫌与中国国家安全部合作。黄仁勋只是因与下属发生关系或外遇而辞职或被免职的高管名单中最新的一个。其中包括2005年的波音前首席执行官哈里·斯通西弗(Harry Stonecipher)、2010年的惠普首席执行官马克·赫德(Mark Hurd)、2018年的英特尔首席执行官布莱恩·科兹安尼克(Brian Krzanich)和2019年的前麦当劳首席执行官史蒂夫·伊斯特布鲁克(Steve Easterbrook)。
据了解，马斯克本人与多家公司的下属有过关系，他甚至通过试管受精与 2017 年开始在特斯拉工作的 Neuralink 高管 Shivon Zilis 生了四个孩子。目前尚不清楚马斯克的回复是否是对黄仁勋的认真报价。但如果这位前 Nvidia 首席执行官决定为 Musk 的 Terafab 项目工作，那么 Jensen 可以利用他的努力和专业知识，将其变成 Nvidia 的强大竞争对手。

【原文 English Original】
Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO two weeks after his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy was revealed by intelligence sources and a day after his affair with an Nvidia vice president became publicly known. But hours before this move, when it was just rumored that the Nvidia board was planning to oust him , Elon Musk had already stated his willingness to hire the former Nvidia chief on X . A random X user posted, “Elon please hire Jensen,” to which the billionaire replied, “That would be an honor.” @zerohedge That would be an honor November 12, 2026 Despite the scandals that Jensen is currently facing, he still has the engineering know-how, deep knowledge of the industry and its inner workings, plus multiple connections across the world, which would be extremely valuable for any company looking to break into the semiconductor industry. This is exactly what Elon Musk is doing with his Terafab project, which he first mentioned in November 2025 . Jensen Huang even warned that this was going to be a challenge, pointing out that “the engineering, the science, and the artistry of doing what TSMC does for a living is extremely hard.” Nevertheless, Musk poured his resources into the project, with construction on the Terafab facility in full swing and with plans to hit volume chip production by the second half of 2028 . Musk himself said that the site targets a production capacity of a million wafers a month by 2032. Tesla has an ambitious AI accelerator roadmap , and SpaceX has even touted making its own GPUs in the future . We still don’t know what Jensen Huang’s plans are, but even though he’s no longer a part of the Nvidia board and its leadership, Jensen and his wife, Lori, still jointly own approximately 800 million Nvidia shares through various trusts and LLCs, while Huang himself personally owns around 70 million Nvidia shares. Aside from that, he still has an outstanding invitation from Congress to discuss Nvidia’s security protocols, which could turn into a subpoena if he snubs them, although we don’t know how his resignation would affect the closed-door meeting. There’s also a reported FBI investigation into his relationship with Alice Huang , the Megaspeed executive who was allegedly instrumental in the import of $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia AI GPUs into China and is suspected of working with China’s Ministry of State Security . Jensen Huang is just the latest in the long list of executives who resigned or were ousted from their leadership position because of a relationship or an affair with a subordinate. This includes former Boeing CEO Harry Stonecipher in 2005, HP CEO Mark Hurd in 2010, Intel CEO Brian Krzanich in 2018, and former McDonald’s CEO Steve Easterbrook in 2019. Musk himself is known to have had relationships with subordinates from his various companies, and that he has even fathered four children with Shivon Zilis, a top executive at Neuralink who started working at Tesla in 2017, through IVF. It’s still not confirmed if Musk’s reply is a serious offer for Jensen Huang. But if the former Nvidia chief ever decides to work for Musk on his Terafab project, then Jensen could put his effort and expertise into turning it into a formidable competitor to Nvidia.

title: Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China: White House
zh_title: 特朗普、习近平、普京将在中国举行历史性会晤：白宫
summary: 特朗普、习近平、普京将举行中国峰会海峡时报 特朗普、习近平、普京将在中国举行历史性会晤：白宫 立即报名：洞察亚洲快速发展 俄罗斯艺术家阿列克谢·谢尔吉延科 (Alexey Sergienko) 描绘美国总统唐纳德·特朗普、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和中国国家主席习近平的新波普艺术画作《深圳 26》于 11 月 12 日在俄罗斯圣彼得堡揭幕。 发布于 2026 年 11 月 14 日上午 05:39 2026 年 11 月 14 日上午 09:41 更新 特朗普、习近平和普京将在深圳举行美俄中首次三方会晤
content:
特朗普、习近平、普京将举行中国峰会海峡时报
特朗普、习近平、普京将在中国举行历史性会晤：白宫
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
俄罗斯艺术家阿列克谢·谢尔吉延科 (Alexey Sergienko) 描绘美国总统唐纳德·特朗普、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和中国国家主席习近平的新波普艺术画作《深圳 26》于 11 月 12 日在俄罗斯圣彼得堡揭幕。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 14 日 05:39
更新于 2026 年 11 月 14 日 09:41
特朗普、习近平和普京将于 11 月 19 日在深圳峰会上举行美俄中首次三方会晤。
特朗普计划讨论削减核武器和伊朗问题，但美国官员表示，不会提出乌克兰问题，因为该问题正在与基辅和莫斯科在另一条轨道上处理。
特朗普还将与习近平会面，共进双边午餐，而埃隆·马斯克将与他同行，但不会参加会谈；芯片出口管制和英伟达丑闻预计不会出现。
华盛顿 - 白宫 11 月 13 日表示，唐纳德·特朗普、弗拉基米尔·普京和习近平将于下周在深圳举行的峰会上举行美国、俄罗斯和中国领导人之间的首次三方会晤。
美国官员表示，特朗普希望在 11 月 19 日的三边会谈中讨论削减核武库的问题，并且还将提及他在伊朗的战争，但预计他不会讨论俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争。
白宫发言人奥利维亚·威尔士告诉记者，三位领导人将在中国南方城市亚太经合组织峰会期间会面。
“总统已明确表示，除其他议题外，他将讨论世界范围内核武器的削减。特朗普总统认为，这种扩散非常危险，”威尔士说。
美国官员表示，主导特朗普第二个总统任期的主要冲突之一将成为焦点，但另一个则不会。
一位不愿透露姓名的美国高级官员在电话中对记者表示：“我认为总统确实打算在与习近平和普京的三边会议上讨论伊朗问题。”
这位官员补充说，华盛顿正在与基辅和莫斯科进行“完全不同的谈判”，旨在结束乌克兰战争，他指的是美国特使最近几天与普京和乌克兰总统泽伦斯基进行的会谈。
这位官员补充道：“中国实际上并不是该轨道的一部分，因此在那里进行乌克兰问题的讨论似乎并不合适。”
官员们表示，特斯拉和 Space X 的老板埃隆·马斯克将陪同特朗普访华，但不会参与与习近平和普京的会面。
特朗普还将于 11 月 19 日与中国国家主席举行双边工作午餐和会晤，这是美国总统 2025 年重新掌权以来的第四次会面。
但特朗普没有计划与普京进行单独的一对一会谈。
官员们表示，除其他话题外，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋因与一名所谓的中国间谍有染而辞职的问题预计不会出现在特朗普与习近平的会晤中。
另一位美国高级官员表示：“英伟达的情况实际上不会对此次访问产生任何影响。”
美国也不打算讨论敏感芯片技术的出口管制，而这正是英伟达丑闻的核心。
“我们不就美国的出口管制进行谈判。这些是我们在政府中制定的国家安全问题……我们不希望它在任何国家中出现。

【原文 English Original】
Trump, Xi, Putin to hold China summit talks | The Straits Times
Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China: White House
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
New pop art painting dubbed ‘Shenzhen 26’ by Russian artist Alexey Sergienko, depicting US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, unveiled in St Petersburg, Russia, on Nov 12.
Published Nov 14, 2026, 05:39 AM
Updated Nov 14, 2026, 09:41 AM
Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin will hold the first three-way meeting between the US, Russia and China at a Shenzhen summit on 19 November.
Trump plans to discuss cutting nuclear weapons and Iran, but US officials say Ukraine will not be raised because it is being handled on another track with Kyiv and Moscow.
Trump will also meet Xi for a bilateral lunch, while Elon Musk will travel with him but not join the talks; chip export controls and the Nvidia scandal are not expected to come up.
WASHINGTON - Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week, the White House said on Nov 13.
Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals at the trilateral talks on Nov 19 and is also set to bring up his war in Iran – but he is not expected to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine, US officials said.
The three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters.
“The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous,” Wales said.
One of the major conflicts dominating Trump’s second term as president will feature, but the other will not, the US officials said.
“I think the president does intend to talk about Iran in the trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin,” a senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters on a call.
Washington has a “whole other track” of negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, the official added, referring to talks that US envoys have had in recent days with Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
“China is not really a part of that track, so it doesn’t seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there,” the official added.
Tesla and Space X boss Elon Musk will accompany Trump on his trip to China but won’t be involved in the meeting with Xi and Putin, the officials said.
Trump will also hold a bilateral working lunch and meeting with the Chinese president on Nov 19 – their fourth meeting since the US president’s return to power in 2025.
But Trump is not scheduled to have a separate one-on-one with Putin.
Among other topics, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s resignation over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy is not expected to come up in Trump’s meetings with Xi, the officials said.
“The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip,” a second US senior official said.
The United States also did not plan to discuss export controls on sensitive chip technology, which were at the heart of the Nvidia scandal.
“We do not negotiate American export controls. These are national security matters that we develop in the administration... and we don’t expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we’re there,” the second official said.
Trump will leave Washington on Nov 16 and arrive in the Philippines on Nov 17 for a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit before heading to Shenzhen. AFP
